guidance.heading: 2026 Outlook
section: “Our third quarter financial performance demonstrates the durability of our business model and our ability to generate sustainable growth, margin expansion and strong free cash flow,” said Josh Whipple, chief financial officer. “We remain focused on driving commercial excellence, realizing the benefits of our increased scale and rigorous integration execution as we build on the financial strength of the combined company.”

Whipple continued, “Our full year outlook is unchanged. We continue to expect normalized1, constant currency adjusted net revenue growth of approximately 4% – 5% and adjusted earnings per share of $13.60 – $13.80 for the full year. We continue to expect normalized1 adjusted operating margin expansion of approximately 150 basis points for the full year and to return more than $2 billion of capital to shareholders in 2026.”

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS up 10% to $3.58, in line; 2026 outlook reaffirmed, Worldpay savings target lifted to $650m
results: Revenue jumped 64% to $3.31bn, mainly because Worldpay is now included; on a like-for-like (normalised) basis adjusted net revenue grew a bit over 4%, faster than in Q2.
Adjusted EPS rose 10% to $3.58, just above the $3.57 estimate; adjusted operating margin reached 42.5%.
GAAP EPS fell to $1.06 from $2.64 on deal amortisation, integration costs and higher interest, and last year included a $344m gain on a sale.
More than $1.4bn has been returned to shareholders so far this year, and a $0.25 quarterly dividend was declared.
The yearly cost-savings target from combining with Worldpay was raised to $650m.

guidance.summary: Global Payments kept its 2026 outlook: normalised constant-currency adjusted net revenue growth of about 4-5%, adjusted EPS of $13.60-13.80, about 1.5 pts of margin expansion and more than $2bn returned to shareholders.

items.metric: Adjusted net revenue growth (normalised, constant currency)

points: Worldpay savings come from merging systems, HR and finance, fewer management layers, vendor deals and fewer offices; the $650m is targeted by end-2028.
Normalised growth was about 5% in SMB and 8% each in Enterprise and Platforms; part of Enterprise volume came from one client's testing that will not repeat in Q4.
Bookings for the Genius point-of-sale system more than doubled, and it is being rolled out through 30+ Worldpay bank partners.
No 2027 guidance yet (due with Q4 results); about $4bn of capital return is pencilled in for 2027, with net leverage targeted at 3x by end-2027.
Management declined to comment on reports of possible take-private interest.
